name: scp
description: Copies files between hosts over SSH, with the same authentication and encryption as ssh.

flags.description: Connect to a specific SSH port (capital P — lowercase -p preserves timestamps, as in cp).
Copy through the local machine between two remote hosts (default in OpenSSH 9.0+).

examples.explanation: Uploads file.txt to the server into the user's home directory.
Downloads a file from the server into the current directory.
Uploads a whole directory to a server listening on port 2222.
Uploads using a dedicated key — common in CI/CD scripts.

about: scp uses the SSH transport; paths are optional user@host: prefixes. Since OpenSSH 9.0 the default protocol is SFTP-based, which improves filename handling. For repeated or resumable transfers use rsync; scp restarts from zero on interruption.
useCases: Quick one-off file copies to/from servers.
Pull a log or config off a remote machine.
Push a build artifact during deployment.
mistakes: Using lowercase -p expecting a port specification — that preserves timestamps; the port flag is capital -P.
warnings: scp overwrites destination files without asking. Quote remote paths containing spaces.
distroNotes: OpenSSH scp is universal on Linux and macOS. Windows 10+ ships an OpenSSH client with scp as well.
